body.x: AirDeep (CEO Yoosin Kim) participated in the 'Startup Zone' at the Eureka Park K-STARTUP integrated hall of 'CES 2023' in Las Vegas, USA from January 5 (Thursday) to 8 (Sunday, local time) for a total of 4 days.
AirDeep is a business that realizes healthy air quality and efficient energy management based on an AI air quality management service.

Its IoT-based AI air quality sensor AirDeep analyzes indoor air quality in real time to detect air pollution factors such as dust, fine dust, smoke, and abnormalities. Also, AirDeep's AI algorithm recognizes abnormal air conditions such as fire in a vehicle or a cabin fire by distinguishing the type of smoke (cigarette or e-cigarette).

The solution’s strength lies in applying machine learning and deep learning algorithms instead of expensive and sophisticated hardware. AI algorithms can improve the accuracy of air quality sensing and detection. With AI, it is relatively easy to reconstruct functions and logic, and it is also cheaper than physical sensors.

Additionally, the software-based technology AirDeep differentiates various air quality conditions with greater accuracy, and the detected information is displayed on the sensor's 5 x 2.8-inch display screen. The indicator flashes blue, green, or red to signal good, normal, or bad air quality, respectively, while AI offers guidance about optimized air quality improvement based on the results of air quality pattern analysis. According to a representative from AirDeep, “For example, if there is air pollution from cooking, it would recommend to run the range hood. If smoking is detected, it would suggest not to smoke in that area.

We have been working on fine dust management and AI-based air quality analysis when conducting various projects. In this process, we realized the field of air quality needs to be accessible to everyone, transcending the barrier of languages around the world. That is why we decided to get into this business.”

Having supplied South Korea’s major car sharing services such as SOCAR and PEOPLECAR, the startup has recently partnered with one of Korea’s giant mobile carriers, KT, and initiated the development of an indoor air quality information provider through Smart TV.

The current version of the AirDeep-Home product is able to 1) diagnose and display information of air quality, and 2) use the diagnosed air quality information to send a guided message for optimal air quality management (via the LCD in the product or app). AirDeep plans to implement the following features in the next version: 1) automatic control of air quality manager using the IR remote communication technology, and 2) edge computing.

‘CES’ is the world’s biggest IT trade show and is a place where one can see the direction and trends of the appliance industry of the entire world. Hosted by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA), it is held annually in Las Vegas, USA in January. Having reported on CES for 17 consecutive years, AVING News started reporting news of CES to the entire world since 2006, and conducted ‘BEST OF CES’, which chose the most innovative product and technology, and ‘BEST OF MADE IN KOREA, which chose the best innovative company in Korea. In addition, it vividly relayed on-site issues in CES through ‘AVING LIVE’.

The K-STARTUP Joint Pavilion featured joint participation of institutions like the Korea Institute of Startup & Entrepreneurship Development, Seoul Business Agency, and Seoul Digital Foundation, as well as 51 Korean innovative companies, to enter the US market and discover global partners. In addition, university student supporters of CES 2023 chosen by each university (Kyunghee, Kookmin, Sogang, Chung-Ang) matched to participating companies based on their respective majors and fields of business.
